description.narrative:
Center for Civilians in Conflict (CIVIC) är en internationell organisation baserad i Washington DC som arbetar med att öka skyddet av civila i konflikt. Baserat på CIVIC's egna undersökningar av hur civila drabbas av konflikter utformar organisationen olika insatser för att militära aktörer och fredsbevarande styrkor på olika vis ska skydda civila på ett bättre sätt. CIVIC ger tekniskt stöd, tränar och utövar påtryckningsarbete mot främst militära aktörer på nationell och internationell nivå. CIVIC började att arbeta i Afghanistan för cirka 15 år sedan och organisationen har sedan växt. Idag arbetar CIVIC i huvudsak i Afghanistan, Irak, Nigeria och Ukraina samt med flera fredsmissioner så som i Sydsudan, Mali, DRK och Somalia. CIVIC försöker även påverka internationella organisationer som FN, AU, NATO, EU samt USA att utveckla sitt arbete med att skydda civila. Eftersom vissa delar av arbetet mot NATO och USA skulle kunna falla utanför OECD/DAC:s definition av officiellt utvecklingssamarbete (ODA) har Sida tydliggjort i avtalet att Sida inte finansierar denna typ av insatser.
CIVIC har ansökt om SEK 15 000 000 från Sida vilka de ämnar använda till att utöka sitt arbete till fler konfliktområden samt fördjupa sin tematiska kompetens inom jämställdhet och resultatuppföljning. CIVIC blir en ny partner för Sida och stödet kommer att ges i form av kärnstöd.

The Center for Civilian in Conflict (CIVIC) is an international organization based in Washington DC that works to increase the protection of civilians in conflict. Based on CIVIC's own investigations of how conflicts affect civilians, the organization plans various efforts to ensure that military actors and peacekeeping forces in different ways protect civilian in a better way. CIVIC provides technical support, training and engage in advocacy primarily targeting military actors at national and international level. CIVIC began working in Afghanistan about 15 years ago and the organization has since grown. Today, CIVIC works mainly in Afghanistan, Iraq, Nigeria and Ukraine, as well as with several peace missions such as the one’s in South Sudan, Mali, DRC and Somalia. CIVIC also engage in advocacy to influence international organizations such as the UN, AU, NATO, the EU and the United States to develop their efforts to protect civilians. Since certain aspects of the work against NATO and the US could fall outside the OECD/DAC definition of official development cooperation (ODA), Sida has made clear in the agreement that Sida does not finance this kind of effort.
CIVIC has applied for SEK 15,000,000 from Sida which they intend to use to expand their work to more conflict areas as well as deepen their thematic skills in gender equality and performance monitoring. CIVIC will be a new partner for Sida and the support will be given in the form of core support.

OUTCOME 1: Governments & national militaries reduce harm to civilians from their own operations, take steps to proactively protect them from harm, and adequately respond to incidents of harm if they do occur. OUTCOME 2: Peacekeeping missions reduce harm to civilians in their own operations, take steps to proactively protect them from harm, and adequately respond to incidents of harm if they occur. OUTCOME 3: Civilians, including groups traditionally marginalized, have the tools and training needed to improve their own protection. OUTCOME 4: The field of civilian protection policy and practice is advanced.

sector.narrative: Civilian peace-building, conflict prevention and resolution

description.narrative:
The final narrative report (Dox 030287/22) contains a range of relevant achievements, linked to the the different objectives that have been set up and looking back at the entire activity period. Below are a few concrete examples of results, e.g. linked to the objective of improving policies and practices as this area is of particular interest to a global strategy, in this case the global strategy for peace and human security:
- In 2019, CIVIC secured its first-ever briefing to the UN Security Council during the Open Debate on the Protection of Civilians in Armed Conflict. CIVIC was also instrumental in forming the first-ever Protection of Civilians Week at the UN in May 2018 and has influenced a number of resolutions, statements, and reports issued by UN legislative bodies and Member States. Also, through reports, policy briefs, public and private advocacy, meetings, events, and workshops, CIVIC has been successful in influencing the negotiations of peacekeeping mandates as well as UN peacekeeping policies and practices and strategic reviews. For example, CIVIC undertook intensive advocacy and had a direct impact in shaping the language in the June 2020 renewal of the United Nations Multidimensional Integrated Stabilization Mission in Mali (MINUSMA)s mandate.
- On the country level, in 2017, after two years of advocacy by CIVIC and others, the government in Afghanistan adopted a landmark national policy on the protection of civilians, the first such policy by a country committing to civilian harm mitigation. CIVIC provided technical assistance to the Office of the National Security Adviser during the creation of the policy.
- In Nigeria, CIVIC's work led to institutionalization of a Civilan Harm Mechanism into the curricula of three Nigerian military educational institutions the Army War College, the Martin Luther Agwai International Leadership and Peacekeeping Center, and the Nigeria Armed Forces Command and Staff College.
- After more than 18 months of engagement with the G5 Sahel Joint Force, the Commanding General authorized the Civilians Casualties Identification, Tracking, and Analysis Mechanism (MISAD in French) and approved the necessary steps to operationalize the cell. To illustrate, even if it was in April 2021 and thus after the reporting period, the MISAD was used in response to a rape committed by Chadian soldiers deployed under the G5 in Niger. Overall, the MISAD will help the Joint Force to better understand the impact of its operations on civilians by identifying and tracking civilian harm and analyzing trends, allowing the Joint Force to both respond to harm and prevent future harm.
- In August 2020, as a direct result of advocacy from CIVIC-supported community protection groups (CPG), Kirkuk Police Command (Iraq) established a reliable and free telephone number for civilians to report misconduct by government forces without fear of retaliation. 20 cases were reported and two police officers were dismissed for extortion. Iraq's Ministry of Interior (MOI) officially adopted the initiative and the same mechanism is now used in all federal governorates to report any misconduct by MOI forces.
- As a result of CIVIC's engagement in Nigeria, 84 % of Community Protection Group (CPG) members reported increased confidence to engage in self-protection. A somewhat unforeseen positive result is also that as the CPG's in Nigeria bring different segments of a community together, it has laid the foundation for increased social cohesion. CIVIC has been told by CPG members that CIVICs workshops and trainings have equipped us with basic skills of conflict resolution. The training has helped us to improve unity and coordination among respective members of our community regardless of our varied ethnicity and religion. (Dox document 030287/22, p.12).
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
